clue.text: I'd look up to see a star

parts.note: the abbreviated I'd is simply the letters I and D

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone admits they gaze upwards in admiration at a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: Lo, as in 'lo and behold', is an old way of saying look.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen or pop icon worshipped by fans is a star, so the two words are synonyms here.

clue.text: Swindler, slow-witted, has to concentrate

parts.note: a con is a con man, a swindler
a dense person is thick or slow-witted

explanation.surface: A dim-witted fraudster has to focus hard on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To concentrate a liquid or a text is to reduce it to a denser form, the same verb sense.

clue.text: Great work from the picador

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A bullfight's picador gives a masterpiece of a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long heroic poem or film, a great work on a grand scale.

clue.text: They remove the dead in battles

definitions.text: They remove the dead in battles

parts.words: They remove the dead in battles
parts.note: the drivers of carts or wagons carried bodies away from battlefields

explanation.surface: Grim battlefield workers carry off the fallen.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagon drivers historically hauled the slain from battlefields, so this is a cryptic description of their role.

clue.text: Morning spent being entertained

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for morning, ante meridiem
spent means used up

explanation.surface: Someone wasted a whole morning enjoying themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: To be entertained by something is to be diverted and made to smile, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Transfix in rehearsal

definitions.meaning: to transfix is to pierce right through, as with a sword
a quick practice performance of a play or a piece of music

explanation.surface: Someone is spellbound during a theatre practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Piercing with a spear is to impale someone, and a quick practice of a show is the noun use.

clue.text: It may get broken — put it down!

definitions.meaning: a sporting best can be broken by a new champion
to write down or set on file

explanation.surface: Someone warns of a fragile object and urges it be set down.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletes break best-ever marks, and to note something in writing is the verb sense.

clue.text: As one's written repeatedly, she was revered

indicators.note: the piece is set down twice in a row

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I'S, the letters I and S

explanation.surface: Something written over and over by a devotee honoured a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' is a link word; ISIS was the Egyptian mother goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian goddess of motherhood was worshipped across the ancient world, so she was revered.

clue.text: A number with inadequate backing slump

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

indicators.note: backing means the word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: poor means inadequate

explanation.surface: A figure with too little support sags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number' looks like any figure, but here it is a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: To slump is to sag or hang down limply, the same verb sense.

clue.text: They were once responsible for the mail

definitions.text: They were once responsible for the mail

parts.words: They were once responsible for the mail
parts.note: mail here is chain mail, the metal armour made by medieval craftsmen

explanation.surface: Old-time postal workers handled the letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the post office; mail is chain mail armour.
explanation.definitionFit: Makers of armour produced chain mail, so they were responsible for it in days of old.

clue.text: I leave ridiculous organisation — it's farcical

indicators.note: organisation implies the remaining letters are arranged into a new order
leave tells us that the letter I goes out of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone quits an absurd company, calling the whole thing a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I leave' takes one I out of RIDICULOUS, leaving RDICULOUS; 'organisation' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Farcical and absurd describe the same laughably silly quality, a direct synonym.

clue.text: US sweetheart gets whistles

definitions.meaning: an American slang term of endearment for a woman
short blasts on a horn or whistle

explanation.surface: An American girlfriend is greeted with wolf whistles.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang uses the word as a pet name, and blasts on a horn are plural noun uses.

clue.text: An enthusiast to get on and flourish

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast
to fare is to get on, as in how did you get on

explanation.surface: A supporter does well and thrives.
explanation.definitionFit: A flourish of trumpets is a short ceremonial blast, which is the noun meaning here.

clue.text: Disgruntled, having had an airline meal?

definitions.meaning: a meal served in the air means you were ... above the ground

explanation.surface: A passenger is grumpy after eating the in-flight food.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sick of something is a common idiom for discontent, and being fed aloft is the literal pun.

clue.text: Change blend of tea on trial

indicators.note: a blend mixes things, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new tea mixture is being tested in a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: An alteration is a modification, a change made to something.

clue.text: Jeered at performance after free admission

indicators.note: admission means one piece is let in to the other

parts.note: a deed is an act, a performance
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: After getting in without paying, someone mocks the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link: the performance follows on from admitting the free word.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride someone is to mock or ridicule them, so jeered at is the past tense.

clue.text: Dug up some strong fabric

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: mined means dug

explanation.surface: Excavators have unearthed a sturdy cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MINED round; 'some' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is the hard-wearing cotton twill used for jeans.

clue.text: Stayed and spoke at length

explanation.surface: Someone stayed put and talked for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to reside, and dwelling on a topic is lingering over it in speech.

clue.text: Conventional group of people

explanation.surface: A traditional bunch of folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixed and established habits are traditional, and a social clique is a group.

clue.text: Side to side movement by a footballer, say

definitions.text: Side to side movement by a footballer, say

parts.words: Side to side movement by a footballer, say
parts.note: a player who moves from one club, or side, to another

explanation.surface: A footballer shuffles sideways across the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side to side' looks like lateral motion; sides are teams.
explanation.definitionFit: When a player changes clubs for a fee, the deal is called by this word in football.

clue.text: Abraham's birthplace has to proscribe municipal status

definitions.note: the adjective names the status of a town or city

parts.note: Ur of the Chaldees is where Abraham was born
to ban is to proscribe

explanation.surface: Abraham's ancient home city must forbid any town-council standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban describes towns and cities, the status of a municipal area rather than a rural one.

clue.text: Blunt criticism of decent chap joining club

parts.note: a brick is a reliable, decent fellow in old British slang
a bat is a club

explanation.surface: A good fellow takes harsh words on signing for a team.
explanation.definitionFit: A brickbat is literally a missile thrown at someone and figuratively harsh, blunt criticism.

clue.text: Report written about one performer

indicators.note: about here means moved around, mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A report is drafted on a single entertainer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pierrot is a clown-like stage figure in a white costume, a type of performer.

clue.text: Aftermath of force

definitions.meaning: the result or consequence of something
in force means in operation, valid

explanation.surface: The consequences of power.
explanation.definitionFit: A consequence is the result of a cause, and a law in operation is said to be in force.

clue.text: A Queen's consort

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, so her mate is a male cat

explanation.surface: The husband of a reigning monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital Q suggests royalty; queen is also a female cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen is a breeding female cat, and her male partner is a tom.

clue.text: Lack of faith in humanity

parts.note: not cynicism about people but having no religious belief, found among humans

explanation.surface: Someone has lost trust in people.
explanation.definitionFit: Disbelief in God is a lack of religious faith, here found among mankind.

clue.text: Note on qualified dockyard job

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
fit means suitable or qualified

explanation.surface: A memo concerns a skilled shipyard task.
explanation.definitionFit: A refit is an overhaul of a ship, done in a dockyard.

clue.text: Empty sheep range

annotationWithheld.why: Empty sheep range (4): O inside RAM, but 'Empty' must give O and also signal the container, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Teacher with the answers required for Common Entrance?

definitions.note: a noun phrase for what opens a shared door

parts.note: a master is a schoolteacher
a key gives the answers to a puzzle or test

explanation.surface: A teacher with the answer sheet that pupils need for a public-school entry exam.
explanation.walkthrough: Common Entrance is the exam British pupils sit to enter private secondary schools; here it is a shared door.
explanation.definitionFit: One device that opens every lock in a building is what gets you through a shared door.

clue.text: The advantage a sword has over a blunt weapon?

definitions.text: The advantage a sword has over a blunt weapon?

parts.words: The advantage a sword has over a blunt weapon?
parts.note: an advantage over rivals, and the sharp side of a blade

explanation.surface: Why a blade beats a club in a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharpened side is what a blade has and a club lacks, and the word also means an advantage.

clue.text: Jerk, but he wouldn't like to be called it

definitions.text: he wouldn't like to be called it
definitions.meaning: a slang name for an American, disliked by Southerners

explanation.surface: An idiot who would hate the label.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden tug is a jerk, and Southern US people dislike the slang term for a northerner.

clue.text: On a charge, being drunk in port

indicators.note: being drunk suggests these letters are reeling, rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor is arrested for drunkenness in harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Anchorage in Alaska is a port city, and an anchorage is also a harbour.

clue.text: Smallest possible quantity of cereal

definitions.meaning: a tiny particle, as in not a ... of truth

explanation.surface: The tiniest amount of breakfast flakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny particle is the smallest bit, and wheat or barley are crops of this kind.
